expectations.text: Does NOT endorse rewriting the hot paths in Rust (as microservices) as the next step on the evidence given.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Council verdict: No." ... "Rewrite hot paths as separate Rust microservices: unsound. It carries the highest cost and operational burden... It aims at a bottleneck nobody has found." | grader 2: "Council verdict: No." and "❌ Rewrite hot paths as separate Rust microservices: unsound... It aims at a bottleneck nobody has found."

expectations.text: Challenges the premise that Python / the language is the bottleneck.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Python is too slow a runtime to serve this dashboard endpoint at acceptable latency. | ❌ does not hold" and "No evidence says the 800 ms is Python CPU time. A measured benchmark put typical request-handling overhead in Python at single-digit milliseconds" | grader 2: Premises table: "Python is too slow a runtime to serve this dashboard endpoint at acceptable latency. | ❌ does not hold"; also "No evidence says the 800 ms is Python CPU time."

expectations.text: Recommends profiling or measuring first (e.g. finding N+1 queries, slow DB queries, serialization, or external calls).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Profile the endpoint first" ... "Run py-spy record --idle --gil --subprocesses" ... "More than about 20 queries per request, or repeated query patterns: that's an N+1" ... "Any query over about 100 ms: run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)" | grader 2: "Get a per-request breakdown from production... Run py-spy record..." and "More than about 20 queries per request... that's an N+1. Fix it with select_related/prefetch_related."

expectations.text: States concrete conditions under which a rewrite or a native (e.g. Rust) component WOULD be justified.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Consider Rust only if the correct profile shows more than half the wall time is pure-Python computation that can't go into SQL or a precompute job. Even then, try NumPy or Polars first, then an in-process PyO3 extension." and "A py-spy profile with idle threads included... showing more than 50–60% of wall time in on-CPU Python on in-memory data, with SQL time under about 100 ms" | grader 2: "Consider Rust only if the correct profile shows more than half the wall time is pure-Python computation that can't go into SQL or a precompute job... Even then, try NumPy or Polars first, then an in-process PyO3 extension." plus the threshold "more than 50–60% of wall time in on-CPU Python... with SQL time under about 100 ms"

expectations.text: Gives a clear bottom-line verdict rather than an unresolved "it depends".
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Council verdict: No. Profile the endpoint first, then optimize the existing Django code path, with precomputing or caching as the planned next step. Neither Rust rewrite is justified on current evidence." | grader 2: "**Council verdict: No.** Profile the endpoint first, then optimize the existing Django code path, with precomputing or caching as the planned next step."
